UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                         BEFORE THE
                           FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.            )        Docket No. ER27-25-000

                           MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF
                               INVENERGY TRANSMISSION LLC
           Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”),1 Invenergy Transmission LLC

(“Invenergy”) hereby submits this motion to intervene and comments on the Midcontinent

Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (“MISO”) proposed Large Load Addition Resource Study

(“LARS”) process, filed in the above-captioned proceeding on October 2, 2026,2 pursuant to

Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”).3 For the reasons set forth below, Invenergy

respectfully requests that the Commission direct MISO to clarify that Merchant High Voltage

Direct Current (“MHVDC”) facilities and generating facilities interconnected to MHVDC are

eligible to participate in LARS, thereby ensuring entities capable of providing capacity to large

load customers seeking interconnection to the MISO system are able to do so through the LARS

process.

I.         MOTION TO INTERVENE

           Invenergy respectfully moves to intervene in this proceeding.4 Invenergy and its affiliates

develop generation and MHVDC transmission lines, including the 800-mile MHVDC Grain Belt

Express transmission line, throughout the Midwest region. MHVDC transmission lines are capable

III.        INTRODUCTION

            On October 2, 2026, MISO submitted its LARS Filing, proposing a new study process

under Section 3.12 of Attachment X of MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating

Reserve Markets Tariff (“Tariff”) “to facilitate the cost effective, timely and reliable integration

of new large loads into the system.”5 Under the proposed framework, MISO would coordinate the

study of paired generation and new large loads on an expedited, parallel basis, enabling both to be

brought online more efficiently than under existing interconnection procedures.6 With projected

annual load growth of approximately 1-3% through 2044,7 new processes to facilitate the orderly


5
    LARS Filing at 2.
6
    See id. at 5-7, 11-18 (describing the LARS study process).
7
    Id. at 4.

                                                           2

DCACTIVE-89594348.4
 interconnection of large loads while safeguarding system reliability for all customers on the MISO

system are necessary. The LARS Filing advances these objectives and is well-aligned with the

goals of the Department of Energy’s (“DOE”) Speed to Power Initiative,8 which supports efforts

to expedite large-scale transmission and generation infrastructure to address rapidly increasing

electricity demand while keeping costs affordable and supporting the United States’ AI

competitiveness. The Commission’s Show Cause Order likewise preliminarily found that MISO’s

existing Tariff provisions may be unjust and unreasonable to the extent it fails to adequately

address the integration of new large loads paired with generation.9 To fully achieve MISO’s stated

purpose for the filing and to satisfy the objectives of both DOE and the Commission, MHVDC

and associated generation should be eligible for the LARS process.

        Invenergy is concerned that, as written, the LARS process inadvertently precludes certain

entities—including MHVDC transmission lines and their associated generating facilities—from

availing themselves of this new process, notwithstanding their ability to provide much-needed

capacity to large load customers in MISO. Clarification is therefore necessary to ensure that MISO

does not errantly restrict the pool of eligible participants and thereby undermine the efficacy of its

proposal.

IV.     COMMENTS

        Invenergy respectfully submits the following comments regarding eligibility for

participation in the LARS process. As discussed below, targeted clarifications to the proposed




8
 Department of Energy, Speed to Power Initiative (Sept. 18, 2025) (“Speed to Power Initiative”), available at
https://www.energy.gov/oe/speed-power.
9
  Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal
Power Act, 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 at P 113 (2026) (“Show Cause Order”).

                                                         3

DCACTIVE-89594348.4
 Tariff are necessary to ensure that the LARS process is available to all resource types capable of

serving large load customers.

           A.       The Commission Should Direct MISO To Revise Its Proposed Tariff To
                    Clarify That MHVDC Transmission Lines and Associated Interconnected
                    Generation Should Be Eligible To Participate In LARS.

           As currently drafted, several of the proposed Tariff definitions identify Generating

Facilities10 as the sole type of resource that may be paired with a large load customer in the LARS

process. The LARS Filing, however, is intended to facilitate the timely and reliable interconnection

of large loads to the fullest extent practicable. Achieving this objective requires maximizing the

pool of resources available to serve new large loads. Restricting LARS eligibility to Generating

Facilities alone would arbitrarily exclude other resource types equally capable of delivering

capacity, thereby undermining the very objectives the LARS Filing is designed to advance.

           In addition to Generating Facilities, two categories of resources are equally capable of

serving large load customers—MHVDC transmission lines and the generating facilities

interconnected to an MHVDC transmission line. These entities can deliver capacity in a manner

functionally equivalent to a directly interconnected Generating Facility, and an MHVDC entity

can contract with a large load customer to provide the capacity necessary to serve that customer’s

load. Indeed, under Attachment X, MHVDC Connection Customers’ requests for injection rights

are processed through the same study processes as Interconnection Requests submitted by

Interconnection Customers seeking to interconnect Generating Facilities. MISO’s existing Tariff

thus treats these requests similarly, and there is no basis for departing from that equivalent

treatment in the context of LARS. The manner in which capacity is delivered to the Transmission




10
     Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein have the meaning set forth in MISO’s Tariff.

                                                           4

DCACTIVE-89594348.4
 System—whether directly or through an MHVDC transmission line—does not diminish the

resource’s ability to reliably serve the paired load.

            That MHVDC transmission lines and their associated generating facilities are equally able

to timely serve large load customers is further supported by MISO’s own filing. MISO designed

LARS to “address the electrically proximate large load portion of the [Show Cause] Order, by

pairing generation with large load in the same LRZ.”11 MISO explained that it chose to “anchor”

the LARS framework at the Local Resource Zone (“LRZ”) level, rather than on a more narrow

geographic basis, so as not to constrain MISO’s ability to optimize transmission solutions.12

MHVDC transmission lines can satisfy this same requirement because each MHVDC transmission

line maintains a designated Point of Connection at which it interconnects to the MISO system

within a given LRZ.13 Accordingly, where a large load’s point of withdrawal is located in the same

LRZ as an MHVDC transmission line’s Point of Connection, the large load and the MHVDC

transmission line are electrically proximate under the LARS framework. MHVDC transmission

lines and their associated generating facilities should therefore be eligible to participate in the

LARS process on the same basis as directly interconnected Generating Facilities.

            Invenergy therefore respectfully requests that the Commission direct MISO, on

compliance, to revise the proposed Tariff to clarify that MHVDC transmission lines are eligible to

participate in the LARS process, as set forth in the redline attached hereto as Attachment A. There

is no reason to exclude such resources if they are capable of satisfying all other applicable

eligibility requirements of the LARS process, and their inclusion would meaningfully advance

MISO’s ability to maintain resource adequacy across the region.

12

            B.      MHVDC Participation in LARS Advances the Goals of MISO, DOE and
                   FERC to Facilitate Timely and Reliable Large Load Interconnection.

           Clarifying the categories of resources eligible to participate in the LARS process would

directly advance the objectives of MISO, the DOE, and the Commission to facilitate the timely,

cost-effective, and reliable interconnection of large loads.

           As MISO explained, it “designed [the LARS process] to facilitate the reliable integration

of significant new load and generation on an accelerated timeline.”14 Including MHVDC

transmission lines and their associated generating facilities in the pool of resources available

through LARS would afford large load customers the opportunity to contract with a wider and

more diverse range of resource types to meet their capacity needs. This clarification is critical

precisely because all sources of generation must be available to serve large load. MISO recognizes

that “the challenge presented by new large load growth is not limited to connecting the load itself”

and “[s]ignificant new demand must be accompanied by sufficient resources to maintain reliability

and resource adequacy.”15 The proposed revisions would advance this mandate by clarifying the

range of eligible resource types.

           The proposed fix would also address the Commission’s concerns in the Show Cause Order,

in which the Commission preliminarily found MISO’s Tariff unjust and unreasonable for lacking

generator interconnection procedures and services designed to facilitate the integration of new

generating facilities intended to serve electrically proximate large loads.16 The Commission

emphasized that this deficiency “will result in MISO’s current generator interconnection process

failing to keep pace with the new large loads seeking to be integrated onto MISO’s transmission



14
     LARS Filing at 5.
15
     Id.
16
     See Show Cause Order at PP 113-119.

                                                   6

DCACTIVE-89594348.4
 system,”17 and warned that it would produce “unnecessary interconnection delays, unnecessary

Network Upgrades, and an otherwise inefficient expansion of the transmission system, imposing

unnecessary delays and costs on transmission customers.”18 Ensuring LARS is available to all

resources capable of satisfying its eligibility criteria would more fully address these concerns by

mitigating the delays and inefficiencies identified in the Show Cause Order.

            Finally, the proposed adjustments complement the goals of DOE’s Speed to Power

Initiative, which aims to “dramatically accelerate development timelines for large-scale

transmission and generation projects . . . [and] ensure sufficient power to support American

competitiveness in artificial intelligence while meeting rising demand for affordable, reliable and

secure energy.”19 Ensuring that all capable resource types are eligible to participate in the LARS

process is squarely aligned with these objectives and may, in some circumstances, identify sources

of capacity that can be brought online more rapidly to meet rising demand.

V.          CONCLUSION

            For the foregoing reasons, Invenergy respectfully requests that the Commission consider

these comments in acting on MISO’s proposed LARS process.

Definitions
Interconnection Customer shall mean any entity, including Transmission Provider, Transmission
Owner or any of the Affiliates or subsidiaries of either, that proposes to interconnect its Generating
Facility with the Transmission System. For the purposes of Large Load Addition Resource Study
(LARS), Interconnection Customer shall refer to the entity developing the Generating Facility, or
MHVDC Connection Customer, that will execute the LLGIA or Large Load Transmission
Connection Agreement, as applicable, which may be a different entity from the LARS Associated
Transmission Customer that submitted the LARS Application.

Interconnection Request shall mean (1) an Interconnection Customer’s request, in the form of
Appendix 1 to the Generator Interconnection Procedures, to interconnect a new Generating
Facility, or a request for the Expedited Resource Addition Study for a new generation capacity, or
a request for the processing of a proposed Generating Facility or an MHVDC Connection
Customer’s request as part of a Large Load Addition Resource Study, or to increase the capacity
of, or make a Material Modification to the operating characteristics of, an Existing Generating
Facility that is interconnected with the Transmission System, or to interconnect an Existing
Generating Facility that is external to the Transmission System, or to change Energy Resource
Interconnection Service to Network Resource Interconnection Service for an Existing Generating
Facility; or (2) an MHVDC Connection Customer’s request, in the form of Appendix 1 to the
Generator Interconnection Procedures, to obtain Injection Rights.

Large Load Addition Resource Study (LARS) shall mean the procedure as set forth in Section
3.12 of this GIP for studying an Interconnection Customer’s proposed Generating Facility or
MHVDC Connection Customer’s request in parallel with the study of a LARS Associated Load
Customer’s proposed load.

Large Load Addition Resource Study (LARS) Period shall mean the period of time in which
Interconnection Requests for proposed Generating Facility or MHVDC Connection Customer’s
request are studied in parallel with the study of a LARS Associated Load Customer’s proposed
load. There are three LARS study periods in one year and each study period will run for
approximately 120 days. All Interconnection Customers requesting to join the next Large Load
Addition Resource Study (LARS) shall submit their Interconnection Request to the Transmission
Provider no later than the LARS Application deadline as published on the MISO public website,
which shall be at least twenty (20) Business Days prior to the scheduled kick-off of the LARS
cycle published on the MISO public website.

Large Load Transmission Connection Agreement (LLTCA) shall mean the form of
transmission connection agreement for merchant HVDC transmission facilities set forth in
Appendix 2 to the MHCP, with modifications to reflect the Large Load Addition Resource Study
Process. Unless otherwise provided, all requirements applicable to the Transmission Connection
Agreement shall apply to the LLTCA. A LLTCA is a form of TCA and, where used in the Tariff,
references to Transmission Connection Agreement or TCAs encompasses LLTCAs.

 LARS Application shall be a single submission consisting of the materials required for LARS
processing as required by Section I.D.1.b.ii of Attachment FF to the Tariff as well as the
information required for studying the Generating Facilities or the MHVDC Connection
Customer’s request under this Attachment X (in the form of Appendix 1) to these generator
interconnection procedures. For purposes of this GIP, a LARS Application shall be a form of
Interconnection Request.

LARS Associated Load shall mean a source of electrical load that is at least 200 MW and that is
formally paired with one or more Interconnection Customer(s) that have submitted an
Interconnection Request to LARS proposing one or more new Generating Facility(ies) or an
MHVDC Connection Customer’s request to provide energy to such load.

Interconnection Customers are eligible to receive one hundred percent (100%) refund of the

Section 3.12.7.3
In the event the Interconnection Customer has elected to make its milestones in the form of cash,
Transmission Provider will transfer the Large Load Addition Resource Study milestone to the
appropriate Transmission Owner to satisfy the initial payment requirement of the Large Load
Generator Interconnection Agreement, TCA or other applicable service agreement within the

the Interconnection Customer has not requested withdrawal, is deemed withdrawn, or is pending

Section 11.1
